n: The day is coming that will burn like a furnace; the proud and wicked will be like straw, left with neither root nor branch — no ancestors or descendants. Moroni quoted this to Joseph Smith with slight changes. (Malachi 4 is chapter 3 in Hebrew Bibles.)

f.g: Dry straw left after harvest — burns quickly.

n: But for those who reverence God, the Sun of righteousness will rise with healing in His wings (rays). They will leap for joy like calves released from the stall. Christians see Christ as this rising Sun.

f.g: “Wings” can mean the rays of the sun — or the corners (fringes) of a garment.
Calves let out of the stall, leaping with energy.

n: The righteous will tread down the wicked, who will be like ashes underfoot on that day.

f.w: ashes under the soles of your feet

n: Remember the law God gave Moses at Sinai (Horeb). The Old Testament closes by pointing back to the covenant.

f.w: Remember ye the law of Moses

n: God promises to send Elijah the prophet before the great and dreadful day of the Lord. Elijah appeared on the Mount of Transfiguration, and on April 3, 1836, he appeared in the Kirtland Temple and restored the sealing keys.

f.w: I will send you Elijah the prophet

n: Elijah will turn the hearts of fathers and children to each other, lest the earth be struck with a curse. Latter-day Saints understand this as the work of sealing families together across generations through temple ordinances.

f.w: he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children
smite the earth with a curse
f.g: Moroni’s version: the whole earth would be “utterly wasted” at His coming — the purpose of creation would be lost without sealed families.
